name: Series N700S Shinkansen
description: JR Central introduced a redesign of its high-speed train. Smaller silicon-carbide traction electronics gave its engineers flexibility to configure different train lengths and room for a battery system for low-speed movement during a power outage.

date.label: March 2018
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: JR Central began basic functional tests with its N700S validation train.

evidence.locator: Plan to launch the new N700S rolling stock in FY2020
evidence.supports: The operator dates the start of basic tests on the validation train.

date.label: 1 July 2020
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: JR Central began commercial operation of the N700S on the Tōkaidō Shinkansen.

evidence.locator: Introducing New Shinkansen Rolling Stock N700S
evidence.supports: The operator dates service entry to July 2020.
A participant in the supply chain dates and locates the first passenger service.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated milestone retained here for this design or deployment.

community_entry.rationale: JR Central began commercial operation of the N700S on the Tōkaidō Shinkansen.

links.statement: The N700S combined the train-draft cooling used by some Series N700 power converters with silicon carbide devices. The development team also used a Series N700 train to test prototype converter equipment.

evidence.supports: The traction developers trace N700S cooling to the N700 and describe running tests on the N700 and N700S prototypes.
Fuji Electric independently documents a blowerless N700 converter as well as a forced-air variant.
In 2015 Fuji Electric confirmed evaluation of its blowerless silicon-carbide prototype on the N700.

evidence.locator: Reducing power consumption and Unshakeable teamwork subsections
evidence.supports: The participating supplier confirms the cooling architecture's development and SiC use in the N700S.
